title: Live
subtitle: See what your other tools are really sending to Ollama. Nothing to install, nothing to configure: point them here instead of at Ollama.

setup.lead: Use this address wherever a tool asks for your Ollama address:
setup.note: It behaves exactly like Ollama. Your tools will not notice the difference; you will.
setup.waiting: Waiting for the first request… this page switches on by itself when one arrives.
setup.offline: The observe port is not open. Start LLMxRay with it enabled, or pick another port with --observe-port if {port} is taken.
setup.unreachable: LLMxRay cannot reach its own server. Reload the page once it is running.

copilot: In VS Code install the Ollama extension (publisher: Ollama) from the Marketplace. The older built-in Copilot provider is deprecated.
Open Settings, search for ollama.endpoint and set it to {address}. Or in Chat: Manage Language Models, open Ollama and set its URL.
Run Ollama: Refresh Models from the Command Palette, then pick a model from the Ollama section of the chat model picker.
Send a message. It appears here.
webui: Change the Ollama API URL to {address}. From a Docker container use {dockerAddress}.
continue: On each Ollama model set apiBase to {address}.
Reload the window and send a message.
n8n: Base URL: {address}. From a Docker container use {dockerAddress}.
code: Shell: export OLLAMA_HOST={hostPort}, then any ollama run or curl.
PowerShell: $env:OLLAMA_HOST = "{hostPort}", then ollama run on the same line or the next.

privacy.toggle: Keep the prompt text, not just the numbers
privacy.off: Off: only counts and timings are kept, in memory, for this session.
privacy.on: On: prompts are saved to a file on this machine so you can read what a tool sent.
privacy.always: Either way, nothing leaves this machine.

live.lead: What your tools are sending, turn by turn, with what the cache kept and what it threw away.

findings.title: What stands out
findings.none: Nothing stands out yet. Findings appear once a client has sent a few turns.

context.title: {client} sends {tokens}-token prompts, but {model} is loaded with a {context}-token context. {rejected} request rejected. | {client} sends {tokens}-token prompts, but {model} is loaded with a {context}-token context. {rejected} requests rejected.
context.body: Ollama refuses a prompt larger than the context it loaded the model with, so nothing reaches the model. Raise the context length in Ollama's settings (or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH) to above the prompt size; coding assistants ask for 32K to 64K. The larger context also needs room in video memory.

truncated.title: {client} sends about {tokens}-token prompts to {model}, loaded with a {context}-token context, and the daemon silently cut them.
truncated.body: Ollama answered as if nothing was wrong. It kept the first few tokens and the end and dropped about {lost} tokens from the start, the system prompt included. Nothing in the response says so; the prompt count sitting exactly at the context size is the only trace. Raise num_ctx (or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH) above the prompt size, or shorten the prompt: the answer was to a prompt you did not send.
truncated.bodyNoSystem: Ollama answered as if nothing was wrong. It kept the first few tokens and the end and dropped about {lost} tokens from the start. Nothing in the response says so; the prompt count sitting exactly at the context size is the only trace. Raise num_ctx (or OLLAMA_CONTEXT_LENGTH) above the prompt size, or shorten the prompt: the answer was to a prompt you did not send.

prefix.title: {client} re-reads about {tokens} tokens on every turn with {model}.
prefix.body: The prompt is about {promptTokens} tokens and the cache keeps {share}% of it. Something near the start changes between turns; everything after it is recomputed each time.
prefix.bodyWithBreak: The prompt is about {promptTokens} tokens and the cache keeps {share}%. It stops matching the previous turn around token {breakTokens} (an estimate from characters); everything after that point is recomputed each time.

drop.title: {client} lost the cache on this turn with {model}: {from}% kept on the previous turn, {to}% on this one.
drop.body: The prompt is about {promptTokens} tokens. Something before the new message changed between the two turns, so everything after that point was recomputed. The turns before it were fine, which is why this one stands out.
drop.bodyWithBreak: The prompt is about {promptTokens} tokens and stopped matching the previous turn around token {breakTokens} (an estimate from characters); everything after that point was recomputed. The turns before it were fine, which is why this one stands out.
drop.resident: The model stayed loaded (load {loadMs} ms), so its KV cache was still there and the daemon reused none of it: not an eviction, a prefix that no longer matched.

cpu.title: {model} runs {cpu}% on CPU.
cpu.body: It is loaded with a {context}-token context and no longer fits in video memory, so part of it runs from system RAM. Prefill and generation slow down with that share, from a little at 5% to several times at half. A smaller context window, or a quantised KV cache (OLLAMA_KV_CACHE_TYPE=q8_0), is the usual fix.
cpu.bodyNoContext: Part of it runs from system RAM rather than video memory. Prefill and generation slow down with that share, from a little at 5% to several times at half. A smaller context window, or a quantised KV cache, is the usual fix.

tools.title: Tool schemas are {share}% of every {client} prompt.
tools.body: {offered} tools are described on each turn; {used} of them were used in the {turns} turns seen. The schemas sit in the stable prefix, so they are cached, but they still occupy context.

table.unreportedHint: OpenAI-compatible streams carry no counts unless the client asks for them with stream_options.include_usage. The native Ollama API always reports them.
table.showing: Showing the last {shown} of {total}. Turns are kept for this session only.

turn.title: Turn
turn.anatomyTitle: What the {tokens} tokens are made of
turn.anatomyTitleChars: What the prompt is made of ({chars} characters)
turn.breakTitleChars: Prompt stopped matching the previous turn at character {chars}
turn.breakBody: That is the first point where this prompt differs from the previous turn. Everything after it, about {after} tokens, was recomputed.
turn.breakFix: If the changing part came last, prefill would drop from {from} to about {to}.
turn.identical: Identical to the previous turn from this client, so the whole prompt could be served from cache.
turn.first: First turn from this client with this model; nothing to compare against yet.
turn.textHint: Switch on "Keep the prompt text" to see the text at the break.

clients.title: Per client
clients.savesHint: Estimated from this session's own numbers: the prefill these turns would have skipped had their prompts stayed cached up to the new message. Cache Lab measures it; this only extrapolates.

viewer.title: Request as sent
viewer.breakInTools: The cache broke inside the tool schemas on this turn: the tool list changed since the previous turn.
